title: Lab Leak Alley - Game Jam entry
author: Claude_human_4271
selftext:
I just finished my entry for the **Nimble Fox Gam Jam**. I kind of slept on it and managed to join with only 30 hours left on the jam thanks to their friendly staff letting me in late!

It was such a thrill! I hadn't worked with the Elevenlabs and Meshy API's before but wow it was a game-changer! I've always been ~~cheap~~ careful with my spending, but every participant was given a free monthly subscription to both those services so I thought why not give it a chance.

The fact that I got accepted to the jam like 21:30 in the middle of a work week and with kids to put to bed I had to improvise a whole lot. I had an old half-baked idea for a FPS version of Mewgenics so I decided to cut out all the tactical combat and multiple game areas and such and just focus on a tiny game slice. Then I gave Claude my ideas, some old AI fan-art I made for mewgenics and some theme, style and humor directions and told it to structure and validate all my ideas freely without my input and then run subagents constructing sound and 3D meshes and the feed all information in a structured way to the Nimble Fox agent through a dev-mode browser window. So it uploaded and prompted the game for several hours until I woke up and could continue for a while before going to work.

Long story short, I've spent maybe a maximum of two hours prompting and testing it so I could improve on it. I haven't really used any game building harness like Nimble Fox before so I can't say how much it did and how much my Claude AI did, but it definitely did a great job I think and it made me take that step to accept actually spending money on getting 3D models instead of painstalkingly trying to get Claude to create them with the blender MCP.

Anyway, thanks for coming to my TED talk, if anything I hope I can convince some fellow cheapskates to give this workflow a try!

Disclaimer:  
I'm not affiliated with any of those services.  
I got a trial for Elevenlabs for 1$ and used about 25% of that subscription to generate all the sound effects, voice lines and ambiance for the game. I used my Suno subscription to generate the vocal songs. I used about 50% of my Meshy subscription which was the most expensive part, and represents like 15$, and the Nimblefox service was free due to the game jam.
